newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates- April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates- April 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- UAE chambers of commerce and industry are keen to set up the first-ever Arab organisation to specialise in technology training.
- GCC industry ministers and officials will meet in Abu Dhabi on May 13 for a two-day GCC industrial conference.
- Nigeria Airways will start passenger services to Dubai from May 12 with an initial two flights a week. After Jeddah, Dubai is the second city in the Gulf served by the airline.

- UAE literacy is on the rise. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) said literacy rates for UAE adults rose to 78.2 percent in 1996 from 77.7 percent in 1995. The UNDP also said UAE life expectancy rose to 73.9 years in 1996 from 73.8 years in 1995. It said infant mortality was less than 70 per 1,000.

- Retail prices for some types of fish, meat and vegetables rose slightly in 1996 over 1995 figures, but there has been virtually no change in prices of other essential food items, the Ministry of Planning said.
- The UAE's stock exchange saw an upswing with interest focused on Emaar Properties.

- Sources close to the newly-formed UAE real estate firm Emaar Properties said the founders of the company are to maintain their current percentage of capital amounting to 34.3 percent including a 10 percent stake for the Dubai government. The rest is offered to subscribers.
